items.question: What exalted attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation constitute a great accomplishment
Such accomplishment belongs to the yoginīs
The practitioner may become dear to them
items.inference: One who attains great accomplishment in both enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginīs, possessing the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter concludes after emerging in the moon island?
premises: The teaching has emerged in Candra-dvīpa
The section is identified as a chapter
Its ordinal position is ninth
items.inference: The ninth chapter is completed as it emerged in Candra-dvīpa.
items.plain_english: The ninth chapter, emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self in this fiery posture?
premises: The self is surrounded by fire
The self stands on one foot
This posture defines the visualization
items.inference: The practitioner should contemplate the self as standing on one foot and surrounded by fire.
uncertainties: The exact ritual or meditative context of this posture is not explicit in the verse alone.
items.plain_english: One should contemplate the self as standing on one foot, surrounded by fire.

items.question: What decisive understanding of knowledge has been revealed to the speaker now?
premises: The speaker addresses the god
The determination of knowledge is the subject
It has been made manifest today to the speaker
items.inference: The decisive understanding of knowledge has now been revealed to the speaker by the god.
items.plain_english: O God, today the determination of knowledge has been made manifest to me.

items.question: What comprehensive division of eight octads is sought to be fully known?
premises: There is a division of eight octads
This division is to be fully known
The knowing is sought in an endless or complete manner
items.inference: The speaker seeks to fully and completely know the division of the eight octads.
uncertainties: The precise referent of the eight octads is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: And to fully know, without end, the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How does the wheel become quickly accomplished in the secret place?
premises: A secret place is indicated
The wheel is the means of accomplishment
Accomplishment occurs quickly
items.inference: In the secret place, the wheel is quickly accomplished, as Bhairava is asked to explain.
uncertainties: The specific method by which the wheel is accomplished is implied rather than stated.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how the wheel is quickly accomplished in the secret place.

items.question: Why does Bhairava praise the question asked by the great goddess?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval
He has been asked by the great goddess
The matter asked about is hard for gods to obtain
items.inference: Bhairava praises the goddess because she has asked about a matter difficult even for the gods to obtain.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O Great Goddess! I have been asked about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located within the subtle body?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead
These are specific placements
items.inference: The syllable kṣa is placed at the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ in the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region; interpreted as location in the forehead.
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is at the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa situated in the body centers?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region
The syllable śa is placed in the heart
These placements are given as part of the mapping
items.inference: The syllable ṣa resides in the throat region and the syllable śa in the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the region of the throat, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows after declaring the wheels of the bodily places?
premises: The wheels of the places have been declared
Their meditation remains to be taught
The beloved is asked to listen
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teacher instructs the beloved to hear their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the wheels of the places have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first wheel described and adorned?
premises: The lotus is divine and eight-spoked
It is adorned by the first octad
This describes its meditative form
items.inference: The first wheel is visualized as a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: A divine eight-spoked lotus, adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct must be abandoned through practice to attain equal-mindedness?
premises: Practice leads to an equal mind
Village dharma represents conventional conduct
Such conduct should be abandoned
items.inference: Through practice, one becomes equal-minded and should abandon the dharma of the village.
uncertainties: The exact scope of grāma-dharma is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Through practice, becoming equal-minded, one should abandon the ways of the village.

items.question: What powers arise from this practice, such as distant hearing and bond paralysis?
premises: Knowledge of hearing from afar is attained
Paralysis of bonds is likewise attained
These are presented as results
items.inference: The practice yields powers including distant hearing and the paralysis of bonds.
items.plain_english: Knowledge of hearing from afar, and likewise the paralysis of bonds, O beloved.

items.question: What further attainments, stated briefly, include immortality and transformation?
premises: Immortality is attained
Transformation is likewise attained
These are stated in brief
items.inference: In brief, the practice also grants immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: The nature of parivartanam (transformation) is not further specified.
items.plain_english: Likewise immortality and, in brief, transformation, O Goddess.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled wheel characterized in meditation?
premises: The wheel is the second one
It has eight petals
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire
items.inference: The second wheel is an eight-petaled lotus, brightly illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability to assume multiple forms arises from one-pointed meditative focus?
premises: The practitioner makes forms in many ways
The mind is gone to one-pointed meditation
Focused meditation enables this ability
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power over the three worlds arises when the adept becomes angry?
premises: The adept becomes angry
He can destroy all the triple world
This includes both moving and unmoving beings
items.inference: When angry, the adept can destroy the entire triple world with all its moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: But when angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: The wheel is the third and great
It is associated with nine principles
It functions as a liberator
items.inference: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.
uncertainties: The specific set of nine tattvas is not enumerated here.
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from mastery of this wheel?
premises: Wrinkles and grey hair are destroyed
Seeing from very far away is attained
These are presented as parallel results
items.inference: Mastery of this wheel brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and the ability to see from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: How should one practice in solitude to manifest multiple forms through meditation?
premises: Practice is to be done in solitude
One should make forms in many ways
One must be intent on meditation
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, one should practice manifesting forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, make forms in many ways.

items.question: What result does unwavering dedication to constant practice produce?
premises: The practitioner is intent on constant practice
Such dedication is emphasized
Immortality is produced
items.inference: One who is intent on constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect the death associated with aging?
premises: Non-eating by day is practiced
Death associated with age is the target
The practitioner will go beyond it
items.inference: Through abstaining from food by day, one will overcome death associated with aging.
uncertainties: The exact sense of gamiṣyate with mṛtyuṃ is slightly ambiguous; interpreted as going beyond or overcoming age-death.
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome the death of old age.

items.question: What youthful bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: Practice is constant and yogic
A specific age-form is indicated as two times eight years
The practitioner attains that form
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power to shake the three worlds arises from contemplating a smoky color?
premises: One should always contemplate a smoke-colored form
This contemplation has a powerful effect
The triple world can be shaken
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
uncertainties: The object that is smoke-colored is not explicitly stated and is understood from context.
items.plain_english: Always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world, O beloved.
